thread.title: Nvidia: It's Not Too Late - NVIDIA Corporation (NASDAQ:NVDA)

author: ALT Perspective
title: Nvidia: It's Not Too Late - NVIDIA Corporation (NASDAQ:NVDA)
text:
Nvidia - It Has Plunged But Has It Bottomed? Nvidia Corp. ( NVDA ) plunged following its third quarter fiscal 2019 results announcement and a downside guidance. It might have felt like déjà vu to some, as the share price of Nvidia also fell after the release of its Q2 FY2019 results. The key difference, however, can be seen in the contrasting messages from Jen-Hsun Huang, the President and Chief Executive Officer of Nvidia.
In the earnings conference call for Q2 FY2019, Jen-Hsun declared the quarter as "another great quarter." Fast forward to November 15 , the founder turned defensive in response to a remark from an analyst who noted that Colette Kress, executive vice president and chief financial officer, sounded "a little different" from the tone expressed during the past few earnings calls.
"We were surprised, obviously. I mean, we're surprised by it, as anybody else. The crypto hangover lasted longer than we expected. Prices started to drift down, and we expected to come down much more quickly than it did and -- but -- and when it went down, we expected demand to come up much more quickly than it did. And so I think the channel wanted to protect its price. People were uncertain about crypto, and demand was uncertain about when the price will be stabilized. And so all of that uncertainty, I think, froze the market a little longer than we expected.
Pricing is now down to below prelaunch normal levels. And so I am hopeful that we're going to see demand come back and the sell-through will happen through the holidays. And we're seeing that. And so that's -- the first one is that we -- just we didn't expect it either and we didn't realize the magnitude of it until towards the end of the quarter." - Jen-Hsun Huang, President and Chief Executive Officer of NVIDIA
In my article in August, I warned that market players might want to "think twice" before investing in Nvidia , amid a "less bullish" narrative surrounding the chip maker. I also pointed out that the technical chart of Nvidia looked ominous. Readers who were long the stock generally shared their confidence in a recovery in the comments section. The share price was around $245 then.
Last month, I wrote a follow-up article titled Nvidia: Headwinds On The Horizon . I laid out my rationale and exhorted readers to revalidate their investment thesis for Nvidia (see the partial conclusion from the article in the following quote). The share price was still around $230, some 60 percent higher than the current level. This time around, longs became more detailed in their comments on the reasons for their confidence while others elaborated on why they had become more cautious about Nvidia and the semiconductor sector.
"Existing shareholders would do well to consider if they want to take their profits off the table. Those waiting on the sidelines might want to update their understanding of the company fundamentals instead of adopting a blanket dismissal of the latest developments. A revalidation of the investment thesis is necessary to decide if this is a buying opportunity on just another 'unjustified selloff'."
The share price of Nvidia is now around $144. This is half of the record high of $292.76 established less than two months ago, prompting calls that the stock has probably bottomed and is now a great bargain. Even Citron Research, a former short-seller of Nvidia, deemed the current price level as offering “an appealing risk-reward to investors." I beg to differ. It is noteworthy that Citron is only projecting a rebound to $165, a far cry from the recent high.
Spencer Jakab of Wall Street Journal recently wrote that investors buying General Electric ( GE ) because of the belief that the share price would return to that last, or any other recent high, were making a mistake. The behavior is called anchoring and it is "one of the psychological foibles that part fools from their money." While Nvidia is not GE, the challenges surrounding the former could mean the stock will face an uphill task recovering nonetheless. I elaborate why in the subsequent sections.
It's Not Just Nvidia, Others Have Dropped As Well, Giving Investors Ample Options While the halving in the share price of Nvidia seems dramatic, its industry peer, Advanced Micro Devices ( AMD ) suffered a drop of similar magnitude over the past two months. During this period, others in the same sector have also fallen, as seen from the 15 percent decline in the PHLX Semiconductor Sector Index ([[ SOXX ]], [[ XSD ]] [[ SMH ]]). Even the mighty Apple Inc. ( AAPL ) is lower by almost 20 percent in the short span. In addition, Chinese giants like Tencent ( OTCPK:TCEHY )( OTCPK:TCTZF ), Alibaba ( BABA ), and Baidu ( BIDU ) have also fallen substantially.
NVDA data by YCharts That is to say, an investor has plenty of choices today if he wants to deploy his money to the stock market. Sure, the share price of Nvidia is down by half but there are reasons for this market reaction.
Nvidia's Operating Metrics Are Deteriorating In my earlier article, I pointed out several metrics reflecting the early "signs of slowdown" at Nvidia. A quarter doesn't make a trend, just as one swallow doesn't make a summer. Nevertheless, the Q3 FY2019 results mark the second quarter the revenue has stagnated, after a strong revenue growth stage from mid-2016. While the year-on-year growth is still respectable at 21 percent, that is a sharp deceleration from the over 60 percent achieved just two quarters ago.
NVDA Revenue (Quarterly) data by YCharts Things do not seem to be getting better. The management has guided for the fourth quarter revenue to be only $2.7 billion versus an earlier consensus estimate for $3.4 billion. That is to say, while analysts were expecting revenue growth, the company is likely to generate a lower revenue in the next quarter instead. If that indeed materializes, the 7 percent year-on-year revenue drop would be Nvidia’s first revenue decline in more than five years.
To make matters worse, what the CEO said during the earnings call did not instill much confidence in the accuracy of the guidance. The cautious outlook statement (quoted below) suggested the potential for further downside. After all, the management misjudged both the pricing and the volume previously and the revised guidance was based on the "hope" of the CEO. Could the company be again overly optimistic about the inventory digestion? Could the continued plunge in crypto-currencies lead miners to sell off their chips into the resale (secondary) market and take away more demand for new chips from Nvidia?
"I think it just took longer than -- the pricing took longer than we expected, and the volume increase took longer than we expected. At this point, most of the pricing has come down to its -- and slightly below its prelaunch levels. And so I'm hoping that -- I'm hopeful that now that pricing has stabilized, that customers will come back and buy. I guess when pricing is volatile in the channel, it probably freezes some people waiting for prices to stabilize, and that took longer than we expected frankly. ... And so we'll keep our eyes on it, but our expectation is that inventory levels will come back to normal by the end of the quarter."
NVDA Inventories (Quarterly) data by YCharts At the same time, another important financial metric, the free cash flow, has also declined consecutively. Free cash flow fell from above $1 billion two quarters ago to just $337 million in Q3, dropping 57 percent from the prior quarter. Consequently, the free cash flow in Q3 represented only 10.6 percent of the revenue, down from around 40 percent two quarters ago. Previously, its strong free cash flow generation was touted as a key strength and advantage over its peers. Now that it has weakened, it would not be unfair that the stock price is reflecting this.
NVDA Free Cash Flow (Quarterly) data by YCharts Market Sentiment Could Be Dragged Down Further As Analysts Revise Price Targets Downwards Post-Q2 FY2019 results, I noted in my prior article that the analysts had already turned less bullish with only "a small uptick" in the consensus price target, as compared to substantial raises in the past. This time around, the analysts have become bearish, with several downgrades and price target revisions downwards. More analysts might jump on the bandwagon, with the consensus price target some 58 percent higher than the current price. That would drag down the market sentiment further.
NVDA data by YCharts Of particular interest is that not only is Nvidia removed from the "conviction buy" list of Goldman Sachs but its analyst Toshiya Hari suggested that the market could take several quarters before regaining confidence in the company. The problem is that there are already rampant talks of the economy being in a 'late cycle', meaning that the next recession is probably around the corner.
Thus, investors of Nvidia might not have the luxury of time to see the stock recover to this year's high of $292.76. Even those who bought into the name in the hope of an earnings surprise for the Q3 2018 results boosting the stock just a couple of weeks ago or so at around $200, some 38 percent higher than today's price, could find themselves wanting to bail out of a bet gone wrong.
Investor Takeaway The current price level has attracted many bargain hunters. Even short-seller Citron Research turned bullish on Nvidia, albeit its price target suggests only a $20 upside. The share price has halved but those buying into the chip maker on the belief that the share price would return to that last, or any other recent high, would probably be making an investment mistake. Those buying Nvidia shares in the high $200 were betting on continued strong growth in the data centers and gaming segments. However, analysts are predicting that the revenue for the video gaming segment to register year-over-year reductions for the following three quarters.
It would not be too late for shareholders to decide if they wish to take profit and shift the money to another investment. Nvidia could rebound, with the 200MA serving as a support. However, the same could be said of Apple and other strong names that have fallen in the past two months.
What's your take? Are you long or short Nvidia, and why? Please freely share your insights, thoughts, and let me know if you found this article useful or provide your feedback in the comments section. For further reading, my recent write-up, " Apple: The Shine Is Off , " might be of interest to you.
